transcript.content: hey, i'm berry. tell me your dream however it comes back to you, even if it's just a feeling or a scrap of a moment.
There was water coming in under the doors of the library. It just kept rising.
water inside a library… that's such a strange mix. the quiet of the place and then that slow filling.
Yeah, exactly. It was so quiet, and then the books started floating off the shelves. Hundreds of them, open like birds.
hundreds of them, all at once. that must have looked both beautiful and completely wrong.
It really was. And then my sister was there, in this little yellow rowing boat. She wasn't scared at all.
your sister just there, not scared… what was she doing in the boat?
She told me to get in. So I did, and she rowed us between the shelves.
like the library had become a winding river. that sounds almost peaceful, in a strange way.
It was. And then a whale swam past us under the water. It filled the whole aisle, but I wasn't scared.
a whale in the library and you weren't scared at all. that's kind of amazing.
Yeah, it was so calm. We rowed up to the high round window at the top of the room. My sister opened it.
the high round window… so she steered you there on purpose. what was it like when she opened it?
Outside it was morning, and the whole city was underwater. Just rooftops and the tops of trees.
the city gone quiet under the water, but the light was morning-like. it feels so peaceful and so empty at the same time.
It was peaceful. Then I woke up.
even though it ended right there, that calm feeling sounds like it stayed with you.
Yeah, it did. I've kept thinking about the green glass lamps on the desks, before the water came in.
the green glass lamps… they stood out even before anything changed. what was it about them that you keep coming back to?
They were just on every desk, and it was so still. Then the water came in under the doors.
that stillness before the water… like the lamps were part of the calm too. was it dark where they were lit, or was the room still bright?
I don't remember if it was dark or bright. Just that the lamps were green and on every desk.
it's funny what the dream holds onto. just the color of the light and that it was the same on every desk.
Yeah. And the shelves went all the way up to the ceiling.
those towering shelves… and the first thing you noticed was the water at the doors. how did the water come in, all at once or slowly at first?
It came in under the doors, and kept rising, over the desks.
over the desks, the lamps still burning maybe. did the water make any sound as it rose, or was the quiet still the main thing?
I don't remember any sound. It was still quiet.
even the water was quiet. that's maybe the most dreamlike part of all this.
Yeah, it never stopped being quiet, even with my sister rowing.

so the dream went like this: water came in under the library doors and kept rising over the desks, all while it stayed quiet. the green glass lamps were on every desk, and the shelves went all the way up to the ceiling. then the books floated off the shelves, open like birds. your sister was there in a little yellow rowing boat, not scared, and she told you to get in. you rowed between the shelves, and a whale swam past under the water, filling the whole aisle, but you weren't scared. she rowed you to the high round window and opened it. outside it was morning, and the whole city was underwater, just rooftops and tops of trees. then you woke up. and it never stopped being quiet, even with your sister rowing.

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
You got it right. You didn't miss anything.
so i've got the whole dream now. would you like to see it drawn?
Yes, I would.

there are a few ways i could draw it: soft pencil on paper, gentle and diffused, with a hand that never presses hard. watercolour on rough paper, flowing and translucent, with colours bleeding into each other. flat black ink, bold and graphic, no shading, only black and the paper showing through. or a photograph, like looking through clear water, with the calm of the dream world.

which of those feels closest to your dream, or would you describe it your own way?
Watercolour on rough paper, I think. It felt like that, soft and flowing.

watercolour on rough paper, soft and flowing. i'll start with you.

and since you were in it, i'll draw you too. how would you like to be drawn: as you are, or however i imagine you? you can tell me a little about yourself if that helps.
Just draw me however you imagine. I don't mind.

i'm sketching you and your sister and the whale and the library and the outside and the little yellow rowing boat and the green glass lamps now. everything is being sketched and will appear on the right over the next minute or two. you can say if anything looks wrong once it's there.
I think it looks right.
good. now for the colors. what colors would you like in the watercolour: soft blues and greens, warm sunlit gold, dark ink and paper, or something else that feels right to you?
Soft blues and greens, definitely.
soft blues and greens it is. i'm glad the sister, the whale, the library and the little yellow rowing boat look right to you. the rest are still taking shape on the right.
The whale looked right too. Big enough to fill the whole aisle.

yes, the whale had to fill the aisle, that's the scale of it. i'm glad it landed.

the rest are still on their way, the little yellow boat, the green lamps, the high window and the underwater city. they'll be there soon.
I'm sure they will look right too.
i think so too. it'll come together in the watercolour, soft and flowing.
It already feels close to how it was.
i'm glad it's feeling that way to you. the rest will be settled in before long.
Okay, I'll keep looking.
i'll draw the moments of the dream in order, each one carrying on from the ones before it. they'll appear on the right as they're ready.
Oh, there's only one there now? Which one is it?

that one is you standing inside the vast library, looking over the shelves. it's the first of seven moments.

does it look the way you remember?
It does, yes. The shelves up to the ceiling, the green lamps on the desks. I remember that.

i'm glad that first one matches what you saw. the shelves to the ceiling and the green lamps feel right to you.

the other six moments are still being drawn, one at a time. they'll appear on the right soon.
Now there are two. Is the second one the water coming in under the doors?

The second one is the water risen over the tops of the desks, after it came in under the doors.

Does it look the way you remember?
That sounds right. It rose over the desks. It was still quiet.
yes, it stayed quiet even then. that's the second of seven moments. the other five are still being drawn and will appear on the right soon.
Four already? What are the third and fourth?

the third is the books rising from the shelves, hundreds of them, open like birds, and the fourth is you sitting in the little yellow rowing boat with your sister.

do those look the way you remember?

moments.action: The dreamer stands inside the vast library, looking over the green glass lamps glowing on every desk, the bookshelves towering up to the ceiling, as water begins to seep in under the doors and rise quietly over the desks.
The water has risen over the tops of the desks, the green lamps still glowing beneath the surface, while the shelves remain towering and silent.
Books rise from the shelves into the air, hundreds of them, open like birds, their pages spread like wings above the rising water.
The dreamer sits in the little yellow rowing boat, and the sister sits at the oars, calm and unafraid, as the boat glides between the towering shelves now half under water.
A whale swims past under the water, its enormous body filling the entire aisle, moving silently beneath or beside the little boat; the dreamer watches, unafraid.
The sister reaches up and opens the high round window, while the boat has been rowed to it; bright morning light pours in.
Through the open round window, the dreamer sees the whole city underwater in the morning light, only rooftops and the tops of trees showing above the still water.
